capabilities.untrusted: In an untrusted workspace nothing runs: no Maven, no Gradle, no wrapper, no JDK manager. Detection reads files; every executing command is disabled with the reason.
config.jdk.sources: Where JDKs are looked for, in order. `mise` first because it is the manager every image this repository targets ships. Empty means: only what `java.configuration.runtimes` already lists.
config.jdk.installVia: Which manager installs a JDK: `auto` picks the first of `mise`, `sdkman` found; `none` disables the install offer. Absent: detected.
config.jdk.matchProject: Pick the runtime the build file asks for (`maven.compiler.release`, Gradle toolchain) rather than the newest installed.
config.generate.getterPrefix: Prefix of generated getters (honoured by the JDT bundle's generators).
config.generate.finalFields: Whether final fields still get a setter offered.
config.report.url: Where `Java: Report a problem` opens its prefilled issue. Empty: the issue template of batlehub-vsx on GitHub.
config.log.level: Verbosity of the `BatleHub Java` output channels.
config.statusBar.items: Satellite status bar items by id, `true` shown / `false` hidden. Absent: the satellite's own default.
config.resources.budgetMiB: The memory every declared cap is summed against before a managed process starts (RFC 0003): the pod's memory *request*, not its limit. Never used above the cgroup limit; with no limit nothing is asked.
config.run.stopGraceMs: How long a managed process gets after its graceful stop or `SIGTERM` before its process group is sent `SIGKILL`.
config.resources.warnBelow: Container memory limit under which the status bar warns and the JDK tab explains what gets killed first. Empty disables.
config.inspections.enabled: Show the BatleHub inspections (JDT bundle) as diagnostics.
config.inspections.severityOverrides: Rule id → `error | warning | info | hint | off`, applied before display.
config.maven.configurations: Named Maven configurations (settings file, toolchains, home, env, default profiles). Absent: one per `~/.m2/settings*.xml`.
config.maven.activeConfiguration: The Maven configuration this workspace builds and imports with.
config.maven.activeProfiles: Profiles passed as `-P` to every goal and written where m2e reads them for the language server's import.
config.registry.enabled: Route Maven and Gradle through the BatleHub registry: `ask` once per workspace, `true`, or `false` (removes every trace).
config.registry.url: The BatleHub registry to route through. Empty: the one `batlehub-vsx` is signed into.
config.coexistence: Written by BatleHub Java: your answer to hiding the stock Java extensions' redundant views, per workspace.
config.experimental: Feature flags for what shipped before its phase declared it stable, e.g. `{ "intellijImport": true }`.
cmd.runGoal: Run a Maven goal / Gradle task…
view.welcome: Open a Maven or Gradle folder, or a Java file, and BatleHub Java activates.
task.goal: The goal(s) or task(s), e.g. "clean package" or "dependency:tree"
task.profiles: Maven profiles (-P); absent means the workspace's active profiles
cmd.maven.applyProfilesOverlay: Maven: apply the profiles through a settings overlay (fallback)
cmd.maven.effectivePom: Maven: effective POM (diff against the raw one)
view.inspections.welcome:
The BatleHub inspections run inside the Java language server (Standard mode) once its bundle is loaded — it loads at server start.
[Restart the Java language server](command:batlehub.java.restartServer)
config.completion.chain: Chained-call completion (`config.getServer().getPort()` as one item). `auto`: BatleHub's chains on every completion, ranked, including `int` and `String` results; `shortcut`: the Java server's own chains, on Ctrl+Space only; `off`: none.
config.completion.chainBudgetMs: Time budget of one chain search, in milliseconds (`auto` only). Fewer chains beyond it, never a slower list; `0` is the server's 3 s. Below 30 is raised to 30.
config.completion.chainMaxDepth: Longest chain proposed, counting every segment (`config.getServer().getPort()` is 3).
config.run.defaultMemoryMiB: What a `process` step of a `batlehub-run` declares when it names no `memoryMiB` — the process group's expected resident memory, summed against `#batlehub.java.resources.budgetMiB#` before it starts.
config.run.showTerminals: A terminal per `process` and `server` step of a `batlehub-run`, kept open after the stop so the log can be read. Off: the debug console only.
debug.run.steps: Started in order, each when the previous one is ready; stopped in reverse when the run ends, fails or is stopped. One of `task`, `launch`, `process` or `server` per step — or only `ready`, to wait for something already running.
debug.run.probe: When the step is ready. Absent: a task's exit 0, a launch's start (its exit 0 when it is the last step), a process alive after `intervalMs`.
debug.run.probe.port: Ready when a TCP connect to localhost on this port succeeds.
debug.run.probe.http: Ready when a GET of this URL returns `status` (any 2xx by default).
debug.run.probe.status: The HTTP status the `http` probe waits for.
debug.run.probe.log: Ready when the step's output matches this regular expression.
debug.run.probe.exit: Ready when the step exited with this code; any other code fails the run.
debug.run.task: A tasks.json label or a provided task, e.g. `batlehub-java: maven package`.
debug.run.launch: The name of another launch.json entry, started as a child session.
debug.run.process: The command as an argument array — never a shell string. Runs with the resolved JDK on `PATH` and in `JAVA_HOME`.
debug.run.server: A step kind a satellite registered.
debug.run.memoryMiB: The declared cap: the process group's expected resident memory, not a heap (a JVM at `-Xmx512m` declares about 768).
debug.run.snippet: Ordered steps with readiness probes, stopped in reverse.
config.inspections.sonar: `auto`: SonarLint's findings in Java files join the Inspections view (read, never re-emitted), and its language server is counted in the resource sum; without it, one row says it is missing. `off`: neither.
config.inspections.sonar.estimatedCapMiB: What SonarLint's language server is counted as in the resource sum when `sonarlint.ls.vmargs` names no `-Xmx` (measured: about 600 MiB on a small project; its own heap has no cap by default).
